title: Common leak patterns: timers, listeners, and caches
hook: Memory leaks in JavaScript are forgotten strong references — timers never cleared, event listeners never removed, and caches without eviction that grow until the tab or Node process OOMs.

blocks.text: A **leak** is reachable memory no longer needed by the program but still referenced from a GC root (global, closure, DOM, module scope). **Patterns**: uncleared `setInterval`, duplicate `addEventListener`, **unbounded Map/LRU missing**, **closure over large objects**, **forgotten Promise chains** holding results, **Redis client event listeners** per request.

entries.plainDefinition: Starting point for reachability — globals, stacks, DOM.
Handler keeps DOM or data alive after navigation.
Map grows forever — every key retained.

blocks.text: Production incidents: dashboard open 8 hours — heap grows 2GB from chart listeners. Node SQS consumer leaks closure over message batch — restart every 6 hours. Fix is profiling then breaking reference chain.

blocks.title: LRU with max size
blocks.body: Production caches need TTL or max entries — Redis EXPIRE or lru-cache npm.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Debug globals in production. Per-request global listeners. Memoize without cache cap.

blocks.text: Chrome: Performance → Memory → allocation instrumentation on timeline. Node: clinic heapprofiler or heapdump on SIGUSR2. Correlate leak with deploy — often new analytics SDK or missing teardown in useEffect.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot name three leak patterns. No profiling workflow. Suggests restart instead of fix retainers.

interviewTakeaways: Leaks = unintended strong references from GC roots.
Timers, listeners, unbounded caches are top patterns.
Fix: clear/off/bound cache; prove with heap snapshot diff.
60s: JS leaks are reachable unused memory. Classic: setInterval, duplicate listeners, Map cache no TTL. Hunt: timeline + snapshot retainers. Redis LRU or EXPIRE in prod.
commonPitfalls: Weak: no clearInterval on route leave.
Weak: memoize all fetch results forever.
Strong: retainer path from snapshot to global listeners array.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS 5.2 using Disposable for cleanup — still manual discipline.
